name: NJ-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Rob Menendez running with a large fundraising edge
No Republican on the ballot; minor independent challengers with no fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to the incumbent: a D+15 district, Menendez's $1.96 million raised against opponents with no reported money, and markets pricing a Democratic win near certainty. With no Republican on the ballot and only minor independent challengers, the race stays Safe D.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or major outside spending against Menendez could narrow the margin, though it would be unlikely to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Aristotle Eliopoulos is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Rob Menendez, the Democratic incumbent in New Jersey's 8th District, seeks another term in a seat his party holds comfortably. The district leans Democratic by about 15 points on recent partisan performance, and no Republican appears on the general-election ballot. His principal challenger is an independent, Aristotle Eliopoulos, alongside two other minor candidates, none of whom report any fundraising.

Menendez has raised nearly $2 million and holds about $680,000 on hand, with roughly $913,000 in outside support and no recorded outside opposition. Prediction markets give the Democratic side about a 95% chance of winning. With no public polling and no expert ratings of the race, the forecast rests on the district's lean, the incumbent's financial advantage, and the weakness of the field opposing him.
